source: សៀវភៅ 'មធ្យោបាយប្រើប្រាស់ឧបករណ៍ព្រោះជាជួរ' (How to Use the Row/Drum Seeder Tool), presented by an agricultural extension teacher for the Agricultural Productivity Enhancement Project in the West Tonle Sap area (APPP) / CAVAC (Cambodia Agricultural Value Chain program), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries -- Battambang provincial department, 2014
text: After use, the drum seeder is prone to rust and wear because it combines metal parts (axle, wheels, frame) with plastic drum sections that sit in muddy water; leaving mud and residue caked on the tool encourages rust and shortens its life. Recommended care: rinse mud and plant residue off the tool thoroughly after each use and let it dry, then store it under a roof out of direct sun and rain, since sun and weather exposure is called out as the most common cause of rust and warped plastic drum sections; empty out any leftover soaked/sprouted seed stuck in the metering holes after use, since rotting leftover seed can block the holes and attract pests; and check that the metering-hole rows are not blocked or bent, since a bent or clogged row sows unevenly the next time the tool is used and should be straightened or repaired before then.
